questions.prompt: In the Apostles' Creed, right after 'the holy catholic Church,' what do Catholics profess belief in?
questions.explanation: The Catechism teaches that 'the communion of saints is the Church' itself -- the phrase describes the spiritual bond uniting all the faithful, living and dead, in Christ.
questions.hint: It comes right after 'the holy catholic Church' in the Creed.

citations.reference: CCC 946

questions.prompt: True or False: According to Church teaching, the saints in heaven continue to intercede for us on earth.
questions.explanation: The Catechism teaches that those in heaven 'do not cease to intercede with the Father for us,' offering the merits they gained on earth through Christ, the one mediator.
questions.hint: Their prayer for us doesn't stop just because they've reached heaven.

citations.reference: CCC 956

questions.prompt: Why does the Church honor the memory of the saints, according to the Catechism?
choices: Not merely as examples, but through a real spiritual communion that strengthens the whole Church
Only as historical role models with no ongoing connection to the living
Primarily to mark holidays on the liturgical calendar
Because canon law requires an annual feast for each saint
questions.correctAnswer: Not merely as examples, but through a real spiritual communion that strengthens the whole Church
questions.explanation: CCC 957 teaches that devotion to the saints is more than admiring good examples -- it is a real communion in the Spirit that binds the whole Church, living and dead, more closely together.
questions.hint: It's more than admiration -- the Catechism calls it a real communion.

citations.reference: CCC 957

questions.prompt: Mary is honored as the first and greatest of all the saints because of her unique role in salvation history, expressed in the title given her at the Council of Ephesus. What is that title?
questions.explanation: The Council of Ephesus (431) affirmed Mary as Theotokos, 'Mother of God' -- the foundation for the unique honor the Church gives her above every other saint.
questions.hint: This is the same title Ephesus gave Mary, meaning she bore God himself.

citations.reference: CCC 466
Council of Ephesus (431)

questions.prompt: True or False: Jesus said that John the Baptist was 'the greatest' among those born of women.
questions.explanation: Jesus paid John the Baptist this extraordinary tribute in Matthew's Gospel, even while adding that the least in the kingdom of heaven is greater still.
questions.hint: Jesus said this about his own cousin, the one who baptized him.

citations.reference: Matthew 11:11

questions.prompt: Match each early figure to the fact that makes them a 'first' among the saints.

pairs.right: Mother of God, first and greatest of the saints
Forerunner of Christ, called the greatest born of women
Foster father of Jesus, declared patron of the universal Church
The first Christian martyr, stoned for professing Christ

questions.explanation: These four figures stand at the very beginning of the Church's life -- before there was a communion of saints to profess, there were these first friends of God.
questions.hint: One was stoned to death; one was declared patron of the whole Church in 1870.

citations.reference: CCC 466
Matthew 11:11
Pius IX, declaring St. Joseph Patron of the Universal Church (1870)

questions.prompt: St. Agnes of Rome, martyred as a young girl around 304 AD, is honored by the Church as a model of what commitment?
choices: Religious obedience to a monastic rule
Missionary service in a foreign land
Care for the sick and dying
questions.explanation: Agnes refused marriage and death threats alike rather than break her consecration to Christ -- the Church still holds up virgins who give their whole lives to God in this way.
questions.hint: She refused marriage, choosing to belong only to Christ.

citations.reference: CCC 922
St. Ambrose of Milan, De Virginibus

questions.prompt: True or False: St. Cecilia, patroness of music, died peacefully of old age surrounded by her family.
questions.explanation: Cecilia was a virgin martyr, put to death for her faith -- tradition holds she sang to God in her heart even during her own wedding, but her death, like Agnes's, came by martyrdom, not old age.
questions.hint: She's honored as a martyr, not someone who lived to old age.

citations.reference: CCC 2473

questions.prompt: St. Lawrence, a deacon of Rome martyred in 258 AD, was ordered by the prefect to hand over the 'treasures of the Church.' What did he present instead?
choices: The Church's gold and silver vessels
questions.explanation: Lawrence gathered the poor, the sick, and the suffering he served and presented them as the Church's true treasure -- a story the Church still tells to teach that love of the poor is inseparable from the Gospel.
questions.hint: As a deacon, his daily work was caring for exactly this group.

citations.reference: CCC 2444
St. Ambrose of Milan, De Officiis

questions.prompt: St. Sebastian, a Roman soldier martyred for his faith, is often depicted in art pierced by ____, the wounds he miraculously survived before his eventual death.
questions.explanation: Sebastian survived being shot with arrows and nursed back to health, only to confront the emperor again and be martyred by clubbing -- his first, non-fatal ordeal is what artists most often depict.
questions.hint: This is the weapon artists always show piercing his body.

citations.reference: CCC 2473

questions.prompt: Match each early martyr to the fact they are remembered for.

pairs.right: Young virgin martyr, patroness of purity
Virgin martyr, patroness of music
Deacon martyr who called the poor the Church's treasure
Virgin martyr of Sicily, invoked against fire

questions.explanation: These early martyrs, all venerated since the Church's first centuries, show that holiness in the age of persecution was often young, poor, and female -- not what Roman society expected of a hero.
questions.hint: One was a deacon; the other three were young women who refused marriage.

citations.reference: CCC 2473

questions.prompt: True or False: Early virgin martyrs like Agnes and Agatha were particularly striking witnesses in the early Church because they chose martyrdom in their youth over renouncing Christ.
questions.explanation: Part of what made their witness so striking was precisely their youth -- girls in their early teens who chose death over renouncing their consecration to Christ.
questions.hint: Think about how young these particular martyrs were.

citations.reference: CCC 2473

questions.prompt: Which title did Pope Paul VI give to St. Benedict of Nursia in 1964, honoring his role in shaping Western monastic and cultural life?
questions.explanation: Benedict's Rule, balancing prayer and work, shaped monastic life so deeply across the continent that Paul VI named him Patron of Europe in 1964.
questions.hint: Benedict's influence stretched across an entire continent, not just Italy.

citations.reference: Paul VI, Pacis Nuntius (1964)

questions.prompt: True or False: St. Francis of Assisi founded his order on a radical commitment to poverty, refusing even communal ownership of property.
questions.explanation: Francis took Jesus' words to the rich young man -- 'sell what you have and give to the poor' -- with total literalness, building his whole order on possessing nothing, individually or in common.
questions.hint: He took one Gospel command about wealth as literally as possible.

citations.reference: Matthew 19:21

questions.prompt: St. Dominic de Guzmán founded the Order of Preachers in the early 13th century primarily to combat which heresy through preaching and study?
questions.explanation: Dominic preached against the Cathars in southern France, convinced that ignorance of true doctrine, not lack of zeal, was letting the heresy spread -- his order's approval by Pope Honorius III in 1216 made preaching and study its very mission.
questions.hint: This heresy taught that matter itself was evil, and it spread through southern France.

citations.reference: Honorius III, approving the Order of Preachers (1216)

questions.prompt: St. Ignatius of Loyola founded the Society of Jesus, approved by Pope Paul III in 1540; its members are commonly known as ____.
questions.explanation: Ignatius's new order emphasized rigorous formation, missionary flexibility, and direct obedience to the Pope -- becoming one of the most influential religious orders in the Church's history.
questions.hint: This nickname for the Society of Jesus is still used worldwide today.

citations.reference: Paul III, Regimini militantis Ecclesiae (1540)

questions.prompt: Match each founder to the order or reform they are remembered for.

pairs.right: Father of Western monasticism, later named Patron of Europe
Founded the Franciscans on radical poverty
Founded the Dominicans to preach against heresy
Founded the Poor Clares alongside Francis

questions.explanation: Each of these founders answered a different need of their age, yet all four shaped how religious life would look for the rest of Church history.
questions.hint: Two of these founders worked as a pair, one man and one woman, in Assisi.

citations.reference: Paul VI, Pacis Nuntius (1964)
Matthew 19:21

questions.prompt: True or False: St. Clare of Assisi was a close companion of St. Francis and founded the women's branch of the Franciscan movement, later called the Poor Clares.
questions.explanation: Inspired by Francis's preaching, Clare left her wealthy family to embrace radical poverty herself, founding what became the Poor Clares -- approved and later canonized by Pope Alexander IV in 1255.
questions.hint: This order shares the poverty and spirit of the Franciscans, but is made up of women.

citations.reference: Alexander IV, canonizing St. Clare of Assisi (1255)

questions.prompt: St. Teresa of Ávila's most famous mystical work, describing the soul's journey toward God through seven dwelling places, is called what?
questions.explanation: Teresa pictured the soul as a castle of many rooms, with God dwelling at its very center -- one of the most influential works of Christian mysticism, part of why Paul VI declared her a Doctor of the Church in 1970.
questions.hint: She pictured the soul itself as a great fortress with many rooms.

citations.reference: Paul VI, declaring St. Teresa of Ávila a Doctor of the Church (1970)

questions.prompt: True or False: St. John of the Cross, a close collaborator of St. Teresa of Ávila in reforming the Carmelite order, wrote of the soul's purification in a work called 'The Dark Night of the Soul.'
questions.explanation: John of the Cross described the painful but purifying experience of feeling God's absence on the way to deeper union with him -- teaching so influential that Pius XI declared him a Doctor of the Church in 1926.
questions.hint: The title of his most famous work describes a period of spiritual darkness.

citations.reference: Pius XI, declaring St. John of the Cross a Doctor of the Church (1926)

questions.prompt: St. Catherine of Siena, a Doctor of the Church, is remembered for urging which pope to return the papacy from Avignon to Rome?
questions.explanation: Catherine's letters and personal visits helped persuade Gregory XI to end the Avignon Papacy and return to Rome in 1377, remarkable influence for a laywoman with no formal education.
questions.hint: Her persuasion helped end nearly 70 years of the papacy residing in France.

citations.reference: Paul VI, declaring St. Catherine of Siena a Doctor of the Church (1970)

questions.prompt: St. Thérèse of Lisieux described her simple, humble approach to holiness -- trusting God like a child rather than through great deeds -- as her '____ Way.'
questions.explanation: Thérèse taught that small acts of love, offered with total trust, could sanctify anyone -- a spirituality so influential that John Paul II declared her a Doctor of the Church in 1997, despite her short, hidden life.
questions.hint: This spirituality is about small, humble acts rather than heroic ones.

citations.reference: John Paul II, declaring St. Thérèse of Lisieux a Doctor of the Church (1997)

questions.prompt: Match each mystic or Doctor to the fact they are remembered for.

pairs.right: Wrote The Interior Castle and reformed the Carmelites
Wrote The Dark Night of the Soul
Urged the Pope to return to Rome from Avignon
Visionary abbess and composer, declared a Doctor in 2012

questions.explanation: These four Doctors, across four different centuries, show that deep mystical experience and sound doctrine have always belonged together in the Church's life.
questions.hint: One of these Doctors was also a composer of music, centuries before the others.

citations.reference: Paul VI, declaring St. Teresa of Ávila a Doctor of the Church (1970)
Benedict XVI, declaring St. Hildegard of Bingen a Doctor of the Church (2012)

questions.prompt: True or False: St. Hildegard of Bingen, a 12th-century Benedictine abbess, was also known for her musical compositions and writings on natural science and medicine.
questions.explanation: Hildegard's remarkable range -- visionary theology, liturgical music, and treatises on the natural world -- led Benedict XVI to name her a Doctor of the Church in 2012.
questions.hint: Her talents went well beyond theology, into music and medicine.

citations.reference: Benedict XVI, declaring St. Hildegard of Bingen a Doctor of the Church (2012)

questions.prompt: St. Maximilian Kolbe, a Franciscan priest, was canonized after volunteering to die in place of a stranger at which Nazi concentration camp in 1941?
questions.explanation: When a fellow prisoner was condemned to starve as punishment for an escape, Kolbe offered his own life in exchange -- a martyrdom of charity that John Paul II recognized by canonizing him in 1982.
questions.hint: He offered his life for a stranger condemned to starve in his place.

citations.reference: John Paul II, canonizing St. Maximilian Kolbe (1982)

questions.prompt: True or False: St. Teresa of Calcutta (Mother Teresa) founded the Missionaries of Charity to care for 'the poorest of the poor.'
questions.explanation: Teresa left her teaching order to serve the destitute and dying in Calcutta's streets, founding a religious congregation devoted entirely to the poorest of the poor -- canonized by Pope Francis in 2016.
questions.hint: Her famous phrase for who she served became the mission of her whole order.

citations.reference: Francis, canonizing St. Teresa of Calcutta (2016)

questions.prompt: St. Faustina Kowalska, a Polish religious sister, received visions of Christ that gave rise to which widely practiced modern Catholic devotion?
questions.explanation: Faustina's diary of her visions of Christ as the Divine Mercy shaped a devotion that spread worldwide after her canonization by her fellow Pole, John Paul II, in 2000.
questions.hint: This devotion is now marked every year on the Sunday after Easter.

citations.reference: John Paul II, canonizing St. Faustina Kowalska (2000)

questions.prompt: St. Josephine Bakhita, canonized in 2000, endured enslavement in Sudan as a child before becoming a religious sister in ____, the country where she finally found freedom.
questions.explanation: Sold into slavery as a girl and brought to Italy, Bakhita was freed by Italian law, entered religious life there, and was canonized by John Paul II in 2000 as a witness against the evil of slavery.
questions.hint: She was brought here from Sudan and never had to leave again.

citations.reference: John Paul II, canonizing St. Josephine Bakhita (2000)

questions.prompt: Match each modern saint to the fact they are remembered for.

pairs.right: Died at Auschwitz in place of a stranger
Founded the Missionaries of Charity
Received visions leading to the Divine Mercy devotion
Former slave who became a religious sister in Italy

questions.explanation: All four of these saints lived and died within the last century and a half, proof that heroic holiness is not only an ancient memory but a living reality.
questions.hint: All four of these saints lived within the last hundred-plus years.

citations.reference: John Paul II, canonizing St. Maximilian Kolbe (1982)
Francis, canonizing St. Teresa of Calcutta (2016)

questions.prompt: True or False: The saints of this level -- Kolbe, Teresa of Calcutta, Faustina, and Bakhita -- were all canonized in the 20th or 21st century, not in antiquity.
questions.explanation: Every canonization in this level happened within living or recent memory, a reminder that the Church continues to recognize extraordinary holiness in every era, including our own.
questions.hint: None of these canonizations happened more than about 45 years ago.

citations.reference: John Paul II, canonizing St. Faustina Kowalska (2000)
